chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The deceased is shrouded in five garments: a shirt that is not buttoned upon him, a waist-wrapper, a cloth with which his middle is bound, a cloak in which he is wrapped, and a turban with which he is turbaned, and its excess is cast over his face.

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: Then he wraps him in the winding-sheet, folding its left side over its right side, and its right side over its left side, and he does the same with the outer cloth, and ties its two ends at what is adjacent to his head and his feet. It is appropriate for the one in charge of the deceased in his ghusl and shrouding to begin, when the needed items that we have mentioned are available, by cutting his shrouds and sprinkling the powdered perfume upon them, then folding them all together and setting them aside; then when he has finished his ghusl, he transfers him to them without delay or distraction from him. If he delays the sprinkling of the powdered perfume until after he has finished his ghusl, then let him do with it as we have described; and preparing them completely with all his needs before his ghusl is better. He shrouds him while he is directed as he had been during his ghusl. When the washer of the deceased has finished his ghusl, he performs wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer), then performs ghusl as we mentioned and explained in the chapters of ritual baths. If the one who assisted him by pouring water over him had touched the deceased before his ghusl, then he too should perform ghusl on account of that, just as the one undertaking his washing performed ghusl. But if he had not touched him before his ghusl, then neither ghusl nor wudu (ablution) is obligatory upon him, unless he has done something that itself necessitates that for him, in which case taharah (ritual purity) becomes necessary for that reason, not because of pouring water over the deceased. Then when he has finished his ghusl, shrouding, and embalming with perfume, let him carry him to his grave upon his bier, and let him and those of his brothers who followed him perform salat (prayer) over him before his burial. I shall explain the salat (prayer) over the dead in the chapters of prayers, if Allah Most High wills. The explanation of all this has already passed in full, and the explanation of the salat (prayer) over the dead will come when we reach the chapters of prayers, if Allah Most High wills.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: It is appropriate for one who escorts a جنازة to walk behind it and between its two sides, and not to walk in front of it, for the جنازة is followed and is not a follower; it is being escorted, not escorting.

key_terms.الذَّرِيرَةَ: powdered perfume sprinkled on the shroud
key_terms.تَحْنِيطِهِ: perfuming or embalming the deceased with prescribed substances
key_terms.جَنَازَةً: a funeral bier or funeral procession
key_terms.خَمْسَةِ أَثْوَابٍ: five garments used for the shroud
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the wudu (ablution) performed like that of salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: is shrouded; refers to wrapping the deceased in prescribed burial cloths

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be shrouded and what are the etiquettes and purification rulings related to washing and accompanying a funeral in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith and accompanying legal explanation describe the rulings and procedure for shrouding, washing, perfuming, carrying, and praying over the deceased. It also clarifies the purification required of those involved in washing the dead and the etiquette of accompanying a funeral procession.
